ABOUT THIS EDITION

The Giryama 2004 Edition is the New Testament in the Giryama language, translated by Bible Translation and Literacy (BTL), a Christian organization established in 1981, in partnership with Wycliffe Bible Translators. Translation work in Giryama began in 1989, and the New Testament was dedicated on 18 December 2004. The Giryama (also called Giriama or Agiryama) are the largest of the nine Mijikenda coastal peoples, numbering approximately 751,500 according to the 2009 Kenya census, and they inhabit a large portion of Kilifi County on the Kenyan coast. The complete Giryama Bible was later launched and dedicated on 6 April 2019.

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus. All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.

3:43
2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.

2:15
3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon. The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.

3:47
4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart. Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.

2:22
5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.

3:07
6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2. The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people. When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.

1:02
7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently. The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income. The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"

2:01
8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything. The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface. He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.

2:14
9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well. Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.

3:10
10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me." Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles. Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.

1:02
11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead. He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.

3:39
12. Sermon On The Mount

Luke 6:24

12. Sermon On The Mount

Luke 6:24

Jesus turns to the crowds and walks through them, teaching. He advises everyone how to walk through life in love. And talks of how, out of pride, we often judge others. He implores those who are listening to love their enemies, to actively pray for them. He speaks of offering more than what is asked of you. Do for others what you would have them do for you.

0:19
13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Luke 11:27

13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Luke 11:27

Jesus reminds us that those who hear and obey are blessed.

2:56
14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

Luke 7:36

14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

Luke 7:36

A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee. Jesus tells the Pharisee a story. He says that there were two men who owed money to someone. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50. Neither men could pay their debt. So the lender canceled both debts. Jesus asks which man loved the lender more for what he'd done.

0:43
15. Women Disciples

Luke 8:1

15. Women Disciples

Luke 8:1

Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well. They serve the disciples, using their own resources to aid the ministry of Jesus.

1:56
16. John The Baptist In Prison

Luke 7:1

16. John The Baptist In Prison

Luke 7:1

Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing. Specifically, they tell him about a funeral procession where Jesus sees the widow who has lost her son. His heart fills with compassion. He tells the young man to get up! The son rises from the dead and goes back with his mother. After hearing this, John asks them to go ask Jesus if He's the Messiah, or if they should expect someone else. The messengers arrive where Jesus is sleeping and ask Him what John wants to know.

2:18
17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

Luke 8:4

17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

Luke 8:4

The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd. A disciple asks Jesus why He speaks in parables. Jesus explains the parable to the disciples. The seed that's scattered is the Word of God.

0:55
18. Parable Of The Lamp

Luke 11:33

18. Parable Of The Lamp

Luke 11:33

Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in. He goes on to say that whatever is kept a secret will be brought into the open. And anything that's covered up will be found and brought into the light.

1:58
19. Jesus Calms The Storm

Luke 8:22

19. Jesus Calms The Storm

Luke 8:22

Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water. The whole time, Jesus stays asleep. The disciples hold on tight. They try to keep the boat afloat. Finally, Peter cries out to the still sleeping Jesus. He tells Jesus that the boat is taking on water and that they'll all be drowned. Jesus stands and puts a hand out toward the storm. The storm clears. And the seas immediately calm.

2:16
20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

Jesus and His disciples continue to sail and arrive at Gerasa. A wild man on the shore growls at their approach. Jesus hurries toward him, ahead of His disciples. The man threatens Jesus with the rock. But Jesus just continues to stare at him. The man calls Jesus by name and declares Him to be the Son of God. Jesus asks him his name. At first the man won't say. But Jesus holds out a hand to him. He says his name is Legion. He begs not to be sent back to the abyss. Instead, he wants to go into a nearby herd of pigs. Jesus puts a hand out to the pigs.

2:29
21. Jesus Feeds 5000

Luke 9:1

21. Jesus Feeds 5000

Luke 9:1

Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside. And a great crowd follows them. Peter comes and asks Jesus to send the people away. He wants them to find food and a place to stay with local farmers and villagers. Jesus looks back out over the crowd of people. They want to hear from Jesus and have sacrificed to be there. Jesus considers this and tells the disciples to feed the people. Mary Magdalene points out that they only have a few loaves of bread and two fish. Jesus takes the baskets and proclaims to the heavens and the people, "Blessed is the Lord God, King of the Universe who brings forth bread from the earth."

1:23
22. Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ

Luke 9:18

22. Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ

Luke 9:18

Jesus asks who the crowds say He is. Peter speaks up immediately. He claims that some in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist. Others say He's Elijah. Others say that one of the prophets from centuries ago has come back to life. Jesus solemnly asks who Peter would say He is. Without hesitation, Peter says Jesus is God's Messiah. Jesus stares back at him.

1:45
23. The Transfiguration

Luke 9:28

23. The Transfiguration

Luke 9:28

Jesus takes John, James and Peter up a hill to pray. Jesus walks apart from them, covering His head to pray. But when He does, His appearance changes. His face changes. His clothes become pure white. He starts talking to two men who seem to be with Him. Moses and Elijah speak to Him. One says Jesus will fulfill God's purpose. The other says He will die in Jerusalem. Peter slowly wakes up. He's the first to see Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus. He wakes James and John. They see it too. Moses and Elijah turn and leave, fading away. The disciples fall to their knees and worship Jesus.

2:15
24. Jesus Heals Boy From Evil Spirit

Luke 9:37

24. Jesus Heals Boy From Evil Spirit

Luke 9:37

The crowds continue to gather. They wait on Jesus. Finally, Jesus comes down the hill with Peter, James and John. One man approaches Jesus and begs that Jesus would heal his son. The boy writhes on the ground. The man goes on to say that the boy is his only son. He asked the disciples to cast out the demon. But they couldn't. Jesus gently tells the man to bring his son closer. Two men carry the boy to Jesus. But he falls again into another fit. Jesus comes to stand over him. The boy looks up. And slowly, he gets up. Now, where there were cuts and bruises on his face, there are none.

0:57
25. The Lords Prayer

Luke 11:1

25. The Lords Prayer

Luke 11:1

The followers of Jesus clean up and take a break at a stream. Jesus stands nearby, praying. Andrew asks Jesus to teach them to pray.

2:23
26. Teaching About Prayer And Faith

Luke 11:5

26. Teaching About Prayer And Faith

Luke 11:5

Jesus has just taught them how to pray. He says, "ask and you will receive." He implores them to seek and assures that they will find. He reminds His followers that none of them would give their children bad things when they ask for good things. He says that no matter how bad mankind is, we still know to give good gifts to our children. And that the Heavenly Father will all the more give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.

0:55
27. Woe To Those Who Cause Others To Sin

Luke 17:5

27. Woe To Those Who Cause Others To Sin

Luke 17:5

As Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside he tells them that there will be temptation. There will be situations which cause people to sin. But the disciples should never be the cause. He looks into the crowd and says it would be better for that person to have a large stone hung around his neck and be tossed into the sea. That would be better than causing someone else to stumble in or lose their faith.

0:28
28. The Kingdom Of God As A Mustard Seed

Luke 17:6

28. The Kingdom Of God As A Mustard Seed

Luke 17:6

Jesus tells the people that the kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed. Farmers plant seeds in their field. From it, a tree grows. And when the tree is big enough, birds sit in its branches.

0:29
29. Jesus Spends Time With Sinners

Luke 5:31

29. Jesus Spends Time With Sinners

Luke 5:31

As Jesus sits with a group of people in a village a man walks up and angrily asks why Jesus sits with those who aren't respectable people. Jesus responds that people who are well don't need a doctor. He hasn't come to ask "respectable" people to ask forgiveness for what they do. But He would ask the outcasts to seek and find forgiveness.

1:57
30. Healing On The Sabbath

Luke 13:10

30. Healing On The Sabbath

Luke 13:10

A boy asks Jesus to tell them more about the kingdom. Jesus teaches in the synagogue that believers shouldn't fear. That God is pleased to give them the kingdom. They can feel free to give because their treasure is somewhere else. He urges them to sell their possessions and give to people. He insists that they can make a treasure in heaven that will never wear out. He says that the treasure follows the heart and where it is.

1:38
31. Parable Of The Good Samaritan

Luke 10:25

31. Parable Of The Good Samaritan

Luke 10:25

A man asks Jesus what they should do. Jesus asks what the Scriptures say. The man replies with, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and love your neighbor as yourself." Jesus tells him that if they do this, they will have life. But then someone asks, "Who is my neighbor?"

1:44
32. Healing Of Bartimaeus

Luke 18:35

32. Healing Of Bartimaeus

Luke 18:35

Jesus and His disciples wade through a stream into a gathering of people. A man asks what's going on. He follows after Jesus, calling out to Him. John comes back for the man and helps him back to Jesus. The blind man calls Jesus the Son of David and begs for mercy. Jesus asks what the man wants Him to do. And the man answers that he would like to see again.

2:21
33. Jesus And Zaccheus

Luke 19:1

33. Jesus And Zaccheus

Luke 19:1

Jesus enters the town surrounded by crowds pushing in on Him. Zacchaeus, a short man, tries to see Jesus. But he can't see above the crowds or get through them. He climbs a tree. Jesus calls out to him. He tells Zacchaeus to come down from the tree because He wants to have dinner with him. People are appalled. Zacchaeus is the town tax collector. But Zacchaeus is more than happy. He comes down from the tree and leads the way.

0:42
34. Jesus Predicts His Death And Resurrection

Luke 18:31

34. Jesus Predicts His Death And Resurrection

Luke 18:31

Jesus continues to sit at dinner with His disciples. He asks them to listen carefully. He tells them plainly that they're all going to Jerusalem with Him. And that everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will come true.

1:10
35. Jesuss Triumphal Entry

Luke 19:28

35. Jesuss Triumphal Entry

Luke 19:28

Jesus starts on the road to Jerusalem. Just outside Jerusalem, there are crowds with palm branches and a donkey. He climbs onto the donkey and makes His way toward Jerusalem. The crowds yell and cheer. The people lay blankets and palm leaves down as a path for Jesus. Some Pharisees in the crowd block the path. They tell Jesus to quiet His disciples. But Jesus laughs. He tells them that if the crowds were quiet, the stones themselves would cry out.

1:00
36. Jesus Weeps Over Jerusalem

Luke 19:41

36. Jesus Weeps Over Jerusalem

Luke 19:41

Jesus, His disciples, and a large crowd of followers approach Jerusalem. When it's in sight, Jesus stops and looks out over it. He talks of how Jerusalem could not see and understand a path to peace.

1:51
37. Jesus Drives Out Money Changers

Luke 19:45

37. Jesus Drives Out Money Changers

Luke 19:45

Jesus walks through Jerusalem. Crowds of people move with Him. He enters the temple and looks around. There are men counting money to each other. And people carry around goods to be sold. He continues to look at the people and the business exchange that's happening in the temple. He walks up and overthrows one money-changer's table. Then another. And another. Jesus charges back into the courtyard area and yells at them. He says that the temple is to be a house of prayer. But they've turned it into a den of thieves.

0:45
38. Widows Offering

Luke 21:1

38. Widows Offering

Luke 21:1

In the temple, Jesus watches a widow give all that she has. People in the crowd note how little she gives. They ask for her to give more. But Jesus proclaims to everyone that the widow gave more than everyone else. Everyone else who contributed gave out of the extra money they had. But the widow, even in her poverty, gave everything she owned.

0:59
39. Annas Questions Jesuss Authority

Luke 20:1

39. Annas Questions Jesuss Authority

Luke 20:1

A Pharisee named Annas asks Jesus what right He has to say the kinds of things he says. In return, Jesus asks Annas a question. Jesus asks whether John's right to baptize came from God or from man. Annas turns with other Pharisees and talks to them. So they go back to Jesus and answer that they don't know who gave John the right to baptize. Jesus stares back. He says since they don't know, he won't tell them who gave Him the authority to teach the things He's been teaching.

1:50
40. Parable Of The Vineyard And Tenants

Luke 20:9

40. Parable Of The Vineyard And Tenants

Luke 20:9

Jesus tells the story of a man who plants a vineyard. That man leases the vineyard to workers or tenants. Jesus shares the verse that the stone the builders rejected would become the most important one. He goes on to state that anyone who falls on that stone will be broken. And if that stone falls on anyone, it will crush that person.

0:58
41. Paying Taxes To Caesar

Luke 20:20

41. Paying Taxes To Caesar

Luke 20:20

The Pharisees tell Jesus they know He teaches right things. They say Jesus doesn't pay attention to anyone's status. But that Jesus teaches the truth about God's will for all people. And then they ask about paying taxes. The Pharisee asks Jesus whether or not it's right that they pay taxes to Caesar. Jesus asks the Pharisees to show him a silver coin.

2:55
42. The Last Supper

Luke 22:7

42. The Last Supper

Luke 22:7

Passover is about to begin. Jesus sends Peter and John ahead to prepare the Passover meal. Jesus sits with them and looks at all of them. He tells them how glad He is to share the meal before he suffers. Jesus takes his cup and prays to God. As when He prayed over the bread and fish, He thanks God for the blessing of the fruit of the vine that God brings forth. He passes it to the nearest disciple and tells them all to drink it. Jesus reaches for a piece of bread and prays again. He thanks God for bringing bread from the earth and breaks it. He passes the two pieces to the disciples and claims that the bread represents His body that's given for them. They should eat and remember Him. The cup is still being passed around. Jesus says that the cup of wine is a new testament in His blood and it's shed for them.

2:29
43. Upper Room Teaching

Luke 22:24

43. Upper Room Teaching

Luke 22:24

Jesus sits after sharing the bread and wine, sealing a new covenant with His followers, and revealing that there is a traitor among them. He passes on one last specific teaching to His disciples. The disciples listen solemnly. He tells them that the greatest of them must be like the least of them. And the leader must be like the servant. He asks which one is actually greater: the one who sits down at the table or the one who serves? He says that the one who sits is greater. But then He points out that He Himself came as one who serves.

4:22
44. Jesus Is Betrayed And Arrested

Luke 22:39

44. Jesus Is Betrayed And Arrested

Luke 22:39

The council of the Jewish elders meets to see how they can get rid of Jesus. Meanwhile, Jesus sits with the rest of His followers and tells them to pray against temptation. Judas arrives at the council and counts out his pieces of silver. Jesus walks off alone so that He can pray. He asks His Heavenly Father to take the burden of His cup away from Him. But He says He'd rather have God's will than His own be done. As Jesus continues to pray, His sweat became like great drops of blood. He rises from prayer and returns to the disciples. But they're asleep. A crowd of Jews approaches Him. Judas leads the way and gets close to Jesus. He kisses Him on the cheek. The disciples lunge forward asking if they should go to battle. Peter runs forward and cuts the ear off one of the men. Jesus heals the man and stops the brawl. He asks why they come with clubs. And Jesus is arrested.

2:23
45. Peter Disowns Jesus

Luke 22:54

45. Peter Disowns Jesus

Luke 22:54

Jesus is taken to the house of the high priest and guarded by temple guards. They push Him and take His clothing in the courtyard. Peter watches from close by. Peter is recognized, but denies that He knows Jesus. As dawn approaches, a rooster crows. Jesus looks over to Peter. Peter walks away, undone by his denials.

1:58
46. Jesus Is Mocked And Questioned

Luke 22:66

46. Jesus Is Mocked And Questioned

Luke 22:66

Jesus gets beaten by the temple guards. A man tells the guards to bring Jesus in to see the council. Annas and Caiaphas enter. The room is full of other Jewish men. They want to know if Jesus is the Messiah. Jesus only replies that if He tells them, the council won't believe Him. He says the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of God. They ask if He is the Son of God. Jesus replies that they say He is. They don't know what to make of His answer. One of them stands and acts as a witness. Everyone heard His replies. The council decides to take Him to Pilate.

1:43
47. Jesus Is Brought To Pilate

Luke 23:1

47. Jesus Is Brought To Pilate

Luke 23:1

Roman guards open the gates and take Jesus. They march through the courtyard followed by the crowd. Pontius Pilate marches out. He's known as the most vicious Roman governor, responsible for the crucifixion of thousands. Pilate demands to know what they want. The Jewish crowd yells that Jesus is confusing their people and that Jesus upset the temple market. They demand a sentence from Pilate. Pilate asks Jesus if he is the King of the Jews. Jesus only replies, "So you say.&quot

1:24
48. Jesus Is Brought To Herod

Luke 23:8

48. Jesus Is Brought To Herod

Luke 23:8

Jesus is escorted into Herod's presence. Herod looks Him up and down then asks, "Who is it that you say you are?" Jesus remains silent. Herod says that he's heard that Jesus can perform miracles and signs. Herod demands that Jesus do something for him. But Jesus stays silent and unmoving.

2:56
49. Jesus Is Sentenced

Luke 23:13

49. Jesus Is Sentenced

Luke 23:13

Jesus is dragged from Herod's palace. Jesus and the crowds come back to Pilate's courtyard. He sits in the judgment seat and says he will only order that Jesus be scourged. The council speaks up again. They remind Pilate that he is supposed to release one man to the Jews during the Passover Festival. The guards tie Jesus to a pole in the center of the courtyard and start to whip Him with cat o' nine tails that rip the flesh from His back. Pilate watches the courtyard warily before he leaves. Pilate makes his way back with a scroll. Jesus is released and dragged back in front of Pilate. He drops the crucifixion judgment at Jesus's feet.

3:34
50. Jesus Carries His Cross

Luke 23:26

50. Jesus Carries His Cross

Luke 23:26

Jesus carries His own cross beam through the streets. The Roman guards beat back those in their path. Jesus continues to struggle under the weight of the beam. He collapses in the street, falling to His knees. A Roman guard looks over the crowd and sees a big man. He is forced to carry the beam while Jesus stumbles along. The crowds yell angrily. But some mourn. Jesus urges them to weep for themselves because there are harder times coming. The Romans push Jesus along after them, prodding Him forward when He stops or stumbles.

2:49
51. Jesus Is Crucified

Luke 23:32

51. Jesus Is Crucified

Luke 23:32

They arrive at the place where the crosses are being set up. Others are being tied to their crosses. Jesus is stripped and led to His own cross. They throw Him down on it. There are cries as the others are nailed to their crosses. The nails are hammered through Jesus's wrists and feet as He screams. Then slowly, the crosses are erected as Romans pulls the ropes. Jesus is lifted high in the air. He hangs on the cross, tired and in pain. He prays for those in the crowd. He asks God to forgive them because they don't know what they do. The crowd murmurs at the feet of the cross. Annas and Caiaphas comment that He saved others. They wonder why He doesn't save Himself. The crowd starts to jeer. They urge Him to save Himself. But He doesn't.

0:56
52. Soldiers Gamble For Jesuss Clothes

John 19:23

52. Soldiers Gamble For Jesuss Clothes

John 19:23

As Jesus continues to hang on the cross, the crowd watches in silence. The Roman guards gather around the cross and watch Jesus. A Roman claims that the clothing is no regular garment. He tosses it to the group of guards. They yell and debate who will get it. One suggests they play, or gamble, for it.

1:06
53. Sign On The Cross

Luke 23:38

53. Sign On The Cross

Luke 23:38

The Roman guard takes a sign and hammers it above Jesus's head. The crowd erupts with laughing and yelling. The guard tries to give Him vinegar from a sponge. The guard insists He save Himself if He's really King of the Jews. The crowd continues to yell. But there are a few who look on and cry.

1:40
54. Crucified Convicts

Luke 23:39

54. Crucified Convicts

Luke 23:39

Jesus hangs between two other men. His disciples watch, helpless. One of the men on a cross asks if Jesus is the Messiah. He tells Him to save Himself and them. The other man on a cross tells him that Jesus receives the same sentence as those who are guilty. But He did nothing wrong. The man asks Jesus to remember him when he comes back as King. Jesus promises the man that he will be in paradise with Jesus.

1:45
55. Death Of Jesus

Luke 23:44

55. Death Of Jesus

Luke 23:44

Jesus continues to hang on the cross. Darkness comes over everything. The veil in the temple is torn right down the middle. Jesus breathes heavily. He prays and gives up His spirit willingly into the Father’s hand. And then He dies.

2:00
56. Burial Of Jesus

Luke 23:50

56. Burial Of Jesus

Luke 23:50

Joseph of Arimathea asks Pontius Pilate for permission to bury Jesus in a tomb. He receives permission. He and a servant carry the body into the tomb and lay it down on a rocky shelf. Joseph covers the exposed, bloody foot of Jesus and sprinkles dirt on Him.

1:28
57. Angels At The Tomb

Luke 24:1

57. Angels At The Tomb

Luke 24:1

The sun rises the Sunday after the Sabbath. The women return with spices they had prepared. But when they get close, they see the rock has been moved. Jesus's body is gone. The linens He was wrapped in still lay there, though. Two angels appear and the women bow. They ask why the women look for someone living in the place of the dead. The angels state that Jesus has risen.

1:22
58. The Tomb Is Empty

Luke 24:9

58. The Tomb Is Empty

Luke 24:9

Mary Magdalene rushes into a room full of disciples. She tells the men the stone has been rolled away. And that when she and the others went into the tomb, the body was gone. Joanna speaks of the angels. She says there were two shining men. And they told the women not to look for the living among the dead. Peter rushes away and to the tomb. He runs in and walks right to the rocky shelf. But there's no body. There's only the linen. He kneels and takes it in his hands. He shuffles it, looking through it. But after a moment he stops. He sighs and bows his head.

1:55
59. Resurrected Jesus Appears

Luke 24:35

59. Resurrected Jesus Appears

Luke 24:35

John and others return to the room where Jesus's followers have gathered. They come in saying that Jesus has indeed risen. John says Jesus appeared to Simon on the road. Simon talks about how they didn't recognize Jesus at first. But when they sat down to dinner and Jesus broke the bread, they knew who He was. Jesus stands in the room with them. He asks why they're troubled and doubtful. He holds out His hands for them to see. He encourages them to touch Him to prove to them that He's flesh and blood. They reach out and touch His hands.

1:15
60. Great Commission And Ascension

Luke 24:50

60. Great Commission And Ascension

Luke 24:50

The men and women follow Jesus down a hill. He says all power has been given to Him in heaven and on earth. So the followers are to go and teach the nations. He tells them to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. He says to teach people how to do everything He taught them. And that He will be with them always.

6:41
61. Invitation To Know Jesus Personally
61. Invitation To Know Jesus Personally

A narrator gives an invitation to know God personally. The invitation is open to everyone. It means turning to God and trusting Jesus with our lives and to forgive our sins. We can speak to Him in prayer when we're ready to become followers of Jesus.

LUMO's Gospel of Mark in Giryama — a word-for-word film of Mark's Gospel with Giryama narration over cinematic footage. Presented as 16 chapters. Giryama is spoken mainly in Kenya by around 1,160,000 people.

Mark 1

The Beginning of the Gospel

Mark 1

Mark 1

The Beginning of the Gospel

John the Baptist prepares the way. Jesus is baptized, tempted in the wilderness, calls his first disciples, and begins healing and teaching in Galilee.

Mark 2

Authority to Forgive and Heal

Mark 2

Mark 2

Authority to Forgive and Heal

Jesus heals a paralytic lowered through a roof, calls Levi the tax collector, and defends his disciples for eating with sinners and picking grain on the Sabbath.

Mark 3

Choosing the Twelve

Mark 3

Mark 3

Choosing the Twelve

Jesus heals on the Sabbath, appoints twelve apostles, and is accused of casting out demons by the power of Beelzebul. He redefines his true family.

Mark 4

Parables and the Storm

Mark 4

Mark 4

Parables and the Storm

Jesus teaches in parables — the sower, the lamp, the growing seed, and the mustard seed. He calms a fierce storm on the Sea of Galilee.

Mark 5

Power Over Demons, Disease, and Death

Mark 5

Mark 5

Power Over Demons, Disease, and Death

Jesus casts out a legion of demons, heals a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years, and raises Jairus' daughter from death.

Mark 6

Rejection, Mission, and Miracles

Mark 6

Mark 6

Rejection, Mission, and Miracles

Jesus is rejected in Nazareth, sends out the twelve, and Herod executes John the Baptist. Jesus feeds five thousand and walks on water.

Mark 7

Traditions and True Purity

Mark 7

Mark 7

Traditions and True Purity

Jesus challenges the Pharisees' traditions about ceremonial washing, teaches that defilement comes from within, and heals a Syrophoenician woman's daughter.

Mark 8

Peter's Confession and the Way of the Cross

Mark 8

Mark 8

Peter's Confession and the Way of the Cross

Jesus feeds four thousand, heals a blind man, and Peter confesses him as the Christ. Jesus begins to teach about his coming suffering and death.

Mark 9

The Transfiguration and Teaching on Discipleship

Mark 9

Mark 9

The Transfiguration and Teaching on Discipleship

Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John. He heals a boy with an unclean spirit and teaches about servanthood and avoiding sin.

Mark 10

Teaching on the Way to Jerusalem

Mark 10

Mark 10

Teaching on the Way to Jerusalem

Jesus teaches about divorce, blesses children, challenges the rich man, predicts his death again, and heals blind Bartimaeus near Jericho.

Mark 11

The Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing

Mark 11

Mark 11

The Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing

Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey to shouts of 'Hosanna,' curses a barren fig tree, drives out the money changers, and teaches about faith.

Mark 12

Parables and Confrontations in the Temple

Mark 12

Mark 12

Parables and Confrontations in the Temple

The parable of the tenants, questions about taxes and resurrection, the greatest commandment, and the widow's offering of two small coins.

Mark 13

The Olivet Discourse

Mark 13

Mark 13

The Olivet Discourse

Jesus prophesies the destruction of the temple and describes signs of the end times, urging his followers to stay alert and watchful.

Mark 14

The Last Supper, Gethsemane, and Arrest

Mark 14

Mark 14

The Last Supper, Gethsemane, and Arrest

A woman anoints Jesus. He shares the Passover meal, prays in anguish at Gethsemane, is betrayed by Judas, arrested, and tried before the Sanhedrin.

Mark 15

The Trial and Crucifixion

Mark 15

Mark 15

The Trial and Crucifixion

Jesus is brought before Pilate, sentenced, mocked, and crucified between two criminals. Darkness covers the land. Jesus dies and is buried by Joseph of Arimathea.

Mark 16

The Resurrection

Mark 16

Mark 16

The Resurrection

Women come to the tomb early Sunday morning and find it empty. A young man in white tells them Jesus has risen and has gone ahead to Galilee.

The Covenant Chapters

The Covenant in Giryama — Lumo Project Films' word-for-word film of the Torah, told through the eyes of Ezra, with Giryama narration over cinematic footage. Presented as 12 chapters plus the full film. Giryama is spoken mainly in Kenya by around 1,160,000 people.

Chapter 1

Ezra Enters Jerusalem

Chapter 1

Frame narrative — Ezra in Jerusalem

Ezra Enters Jerusalem

The opening frame narrative. The priest-scribe Ezra returns to Jerusalem and prepares to recount the foundational story of God's covenant with Israel — setting the stage for the great Torah retelling that follows.

Chapter 2

The Creation of Humanity

Chapter 2

Genesis 1–4

The Creation of Humanity

God creates the heavens and the earth, forms Adam and Eve in His image, and places them in the garden. The first humans break trust with their Creator and are cast out into a world marked by hardship — the entry point of every story that follows.

Chapter 3

Noah, the Flood and the Next Generation

Chapter 3

Genesis 6–9

Noah, the Flood and the Next Generation

As violence fills the earth, God grieves and resolves to begin again. Noah finds favor and builds the ark. The flood comes and recedes, and God establishes His covenant with Noah, setting the rainbow in the sky as a sign for every generation.

Chapter 4

The Lord's Covenant with Abraham

Chapter 4

Genesis 12, 15, 17

The Lord's Covenant with Abraham

God calls Abram out of his homeland and promises to make him a great nation through whom all peoples will be blessed. In a vision and through the sign of circumcision, God formalizes His covenant with Abraham and his descendants.

Chapter 5

The Birth of Isaac

Chapter 5

Genesis 18, 21

The Birth of Isaac

Long after Abraham and Sarah have given up hope of children, the Lord visits them and reaffirms His promise. Sarah laughs, but in the appointed time Isaac — the child of promise — is born.

Chapter 6

Abraham Tested

Chapter 6

Genesis 22

Abraham Tested

God tests Abraham's faith by commanding him to offer his only son Isaac on Mount Moriah. As Abraham raises the knife, the Lord intervenes, providing a ram in Isaac's place — a defining picture of trust, sacrifice, and God's provision.

Chapter 7

Joseph's Dream

Chapter 7

Genesis 37

Joseph's Dream

Jacob's favored son Joseph dreams that his family will one day bow before him. His brothers' jealousy boils over, and they sell him into slavery in Egypt — beginning a long providential journey that will preserve the family of promise.

Chapter 8

Joseph and Potiphar's Wife

Chapter 8

Genesis 39

Joseph and Potiphar's Wife

In Egypt, Joseph rises to a place of trust in the household of Potiphar. Falsely accused by Potiphar's wife after refusing her advances, he is thrown into prison — yet the Lord remains with him.

Chapter 9

Joseph's Brothers Go to Egypt

Chapter 9

Genesis 41–45

Joseph's Brothers Go to Egypt

Years later, Joseph has risen to become governor of Egypt. When famine drives his brothers down from Canaan in search of grain, they unknowingly come before the brother they betrayed. Joseph reveals himself, forgives them, and the family of Israel is reunited and resettled in Egypt.

Chapter 10

The Israelites Oppressed

Chapter 10

Exodus 1–2

The Israelites Oppressed

Generations later a new pharaoh arises who does not remember Joseph. The Hebrews multiply and are forced into bitter slavery. Among them a Hebrew boy named Moses is hidden in the reeds and grows up in Pharaoh's own household.

Chapter 11

Moses and the Burning Bush

Chapter 11

Exodus 3–4

Moses and the Burning Bush

After fleeing Egypt, Moses keeps flocks in Midian. On Mount Horeb the Lord appears in a bush that burns without being consumed and commissions Moses to return to Egypt and bring His people out of slavery.

Chapter 12

The Passover, the Exodus, and the Covenant at Sinai

Chapter 12

Exodus 5–20 and beyond

The Passover, the Exodus, and the Covenant at Sinai

Moses confronts Pharaoh, the plagues fall on Egypt, and the Passover lamb is slain. Israel is freed and crosses the Red Sea on dry ground. In the wilderness God provides manna and quail, gives the Ten Commandments at Sinai, and renews His covenant with His people — calling them to choose life and the promised land that lies ahead.

his 1994 Genesis portion in Giryama was published by the Bible Society of Kenya for the Giriama communities of the northern Kenyan coast. Giryama (ISO 639-3 nyf), one of the nine Mijikenda languages, is spoken by around 1 million people in Kilifi County and adjacent coastal districts, with Malindi, Kaloleni, and Mariakani as major population centres (Ethnologue: nyf).

Scripture work in Giryama dates to the Church Missionary Society station at Rabai, founded in 1846 by Johann Ludwig Krapf and Johannes Rebmann. Krapf's linguistic surveys covered several Mijikenda varieties, but sustained Giryama translation came later under W. E. Taylor, who produced a Giryama New Testament in 1904. The full Giryama Bible appeared in 1954, issued by the British and Foreign Bible Society.

The 1994 Genesis portion belongs to a subsequent revision cycle led by the Bible Society of Kenya, which undertook individual-book reprints of the Old Testament using an updated Latin orthography consistent with other coastal Mijikenda languages. The booklet served Anglican, Methodist, and Pentecostal congregations in the Giriama-speaking districts, as well as emerging use in primary-school religious instruction. Giryama scripture continues to function as a regional standard, with adjacent Mijikenda varieties such as Chonyi and Duruma accessing it as a bridge translation.

ospel of Luke in a bilingual Giryama and Swahili setting, printed in 1892 by the British and Foreign Bible Society for the Church Missionary Society stations on the Kilifi coast of British East Africa. The volume presents the Lukan text in parallel Giryama and Swahili columns, a format adopted where coastal Swahili served as a trade lingua franca alongside the inland Mijikenda cluster, of which Giryama is the largest member.

The translator was William Ernest Taylor, CMS missionary and linguist who arrived at Frere Town, Mombasa, in 1880 and moved inland to Rabai and Ribe in the mid-1880s to work among Giryama speakers. Taylor published a Giryama vocabulary (1891) and collected proverbs and grammatical notes that formed the foundation of Giryama biblical translation. His Swahili work ran in parallel and drew on the Zanzibar revision tradition established by Johann Ludwig Krapf and later Edward Steere.

The 1892 Luke circulated among Giryama congregations at Rabai, Ribe, Jomvu, and Kaloleni. Print runs for CMS portions in coastal languages were measured in the hundreds, and BFBS shipped stocks to the Mombasa depot for overland distribution. The parallel Swahili text gave mission teachers access to the Lukan narrative in both the church language and the vernacular of the Mijikenda hinterland.

ilingual Swahili-Giryama Luke of 1892, a second entry for the same British and Foreign Bible Society parallel edition prepared by William Ernest Taylor of the Church Missionary Society. In this catalogue record the columns are reordered to lead with Swahili, reflecting how the volume was filed when the Swahili text was the primary language of reference at a given mission station.

The parallel format served mission teachers who taught in both languages, giving Giryama catechumens a Swahili equivalent on the facing column for words not yet stable in the emerging Giryama literary register. BFBS issued the edition for CMS use on the Kilifi coast, and the volume circulated between Mombasa, Frere Town, Rabai, Ribe, Jomvu, and Kaloleni. items.title: The Beginning
items.description:
The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus.

All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.
items.description_short: The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus.

items.title: Birth Of Jesus
items.description:
Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God.

Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.
items.description_short: Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God.

items.title: Childhood Of Jesus
items.description:
One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon.

The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.
